tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. - "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name

- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.content:
1	---
2	title: 'Story 6.1 — Send Message & Receive RAG-Grounded Streaming Response'
3	type: 'feature'
4	created: '2026-11-05'
5	status: 'done'
6	review_loop_iteration: 0
7	baseline_commit: 'f6eb83a3c07be75879b88469a6c962785f0eea24'
8	context: ['{project-root}/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-6-context.md']
9	---
10	
11	<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">
12	
13	## Intent
14	
15	**Problem:** Home/Chat is still `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen` — a non-functional placeholder. RF04's core promise (a conversation grounded in the user's own Entries via the real backend) doesn't exist yet.
16	
17	**Approach:** Build chat's first vertical slice (domain/data/presentation) to send a message and stream a RAG-grounded response over SSE, rendering exactly three per-message states (streaming, error, complete). Replace the placeholder screen with a minimal real one: header+drawer chrome reused, a message list, and a composer ("+" → existing `InsertionModal`, text field, send icon).
18	
19	## Boundaries & Constraints
20	
21	**Always:**
22	- Exactly 3 visible message states: streaming (progressive text + blinking cursor, cursor skipped under `MediaQuery.of(context).disableAnimations`), error, complete. Bubble text is never cleared once any text streamed in, even on failure.
23	- `ChatRepository.sendMessage` returns `Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>>`; every other method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (RNF09).
24	- Call the backend only via `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>` (`chat-sessions-list`, `chat-sessions-create`, `chat-messages-list`, `chat-messages-send`) with `apikey` + `Bearer <user token>` headers, never the literal OpenAPI path.
25	- No connectivity → send resolves immediately to `Failure.networkOffline`; never queued.
26	- Add streaming to the shared `ApiClient` (`lib/core/network/api_client.dart`) instead of bypassing it — it stays the one façade every datasource calls through (AD-2/AD-5).
27	- Domain layer (`chat/domain`) imports neither `package:flutter` nor `chat/data` (RNF06).
28	- Chat's state is its own sealed class, never forced into `Resource<T>` (AD-12).
29	- On opening Home/Chat, silently ensure one Chat Session exists (reuse the most recent from `chat-sessions-list`, else `chat-sessions-create` with no title) — kept in memory only, no session-switcher UI (Story 6.2's job).
30	- Reuse `InsertionModal.show(...)` unchanged for the composer's "+".
31	
32	**Ask First:** none identified — session bootstrap is explicitly scoped to an in-memory value (see Design Notes) to avoid colliding with 6.2.
33	
34	**Never:** the retry-tap action / `chat-messages-retry` call, offline composer banner/lock, multi-session switcher, bookmark/save-to-journal button, insight card (all Stories 6.2–6.5); rendering the SSE `context` event's retrieval/citation data; any direct AI-provider call.
35	
36	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
37	
38	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
39	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
40	| Happy path | Session exists, backend streams `message_created→token*→done` | Bubble fills progressively, ends `complete` | N/A |
41	| Mid-stream drop | Connection closes after some tokens, no `done`/`error` | Bubble keeps partial text, status `failed`, generic error indicator (not retry copy) | `Failure.networkTimeout` surfaced, no exception escapes |
42	| In-band `error` event | SSE emits `error` with a taxonomy code | Message marked `failed` | `Failure.fromCode(code, message)` |
43	| Send while offline | No connectivity | Send fails immediately, bubble marked `failed` | `Failure.networkOffline` |
44	| Bootstrap failure | `chat-sessions-list`/`create` fails on screen open | Screen shows a generic error state, not infinite spinner | Failure surfaced, no crash |
45	
46	</frozen-after-approval>
47	
48	## Code Map
49	
50	- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:1156-1306` -- `chat.messages.list/send/retry`, `chat.sessions.list/create`: x-cerne-function names, request/response schemas, SSE order `message_created→context→token*→done|error` (no per-event field schema given).
51	- `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md` -- closed 13-code set; `NETWORK_OFFLINE` never an actual HTTP response.
52	- `docs/input/requirements.md:30-35` -- RF04 AC (3 states; dropped stream keeps partial text); `:170-179` -- endpoint-to-RF04 table.
53	- `lib/core/failure/failure.dart:14-83` -- sealed `Failure`, `retryable`, `Failure.fromCode`.
54	- `lib/core/resource.dart:1-33` -- doc comment explicitly excludes RF04's chat stream from `Resource<T>`.
55	- `lib/core/network/api_client.dart:27-148` -- façade to extend with a streaming method; mirror `_send`/`_mapDioException` (88-127) for error mapping.
56	- `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart:84-92` -- feature-registration call order to extend with `registerChatFeature()`.
57	- `lib/features/entries/entries_injection.dart:20-84`, `entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart`, `entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart`, `entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart` -- DI/Hive-box convention and Either-construction/DTO-parse pattern to mirror for chat's non-streaming calls.
58	- `lib/core/design_tokens.dart:27,39,51,60,66,90,201-210` -- `colorAccent`, `colorSurfaceElevated`, `colorError`, `colorInfoOffline`, `colorChatBubbleUser`, `colorErrorBg`, radii.
59	- `lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal.dart:56-78` -- Reduce Motion pattern to mirror for the streaming cursor.

## Intent

**Problem:** Home/Chat is still `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen` — a non-functional placeholder. RF04's core promise (a conversation grounded in the user's own Entries via the real backend) doesn't exist yet.

**Approach:** Build chat's first vertical slice (domain/data/presentation) to send a message and stream a RAG-grounded response over SSE, rendering exactly three per-message states (streaming, error, complete). Replace the placeholder screen with a minimal real one: header+drawer chrome reused, a message list, and a composer ("+" → existing `InsertionModal`, text field, send icon).

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Exactly 3 visible message states: streaming (progressive text + blinking cursor, cursor skipped under `MediaQuery.of(context).disableAnimations`), error, complete. Bubble text is never cleared once any text streamed in, even on failure.
- `ChatRepository.sendMessage` returns `Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>>`; every other method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (RNF09).
- Call the backend only via `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>` (`chat-sessions-list`, `chat-sessions-create`, `chat-messages-list`, `chat-messages-send`) with `apikey` + `Bearer <user token>` headers, never the literal OpenAPI path.
- No connectivity → send resolves immediately to `Failure.networkOffline`; never queued.
- Add streaming to the shared `ApiClient` (`lib/core/network/api_client.dart`) instead of bypassing it — it stays the one façade every datasource calls through (AD-2/AD-5).
- Domain layer (`chat/domain`) imports neither `package:flutter` nor `chat/data` (RNF06).
- Chat's state is its own sealed class, never forced into `Resource<T>` (AD-12).
- On opening Home/Chat, silently ensure one Chat Session exists (reuse the most recent from `chat-sessions-list`, else `chat-sessions-create` with no title) — kept in memory only, no session-switcher UI (Story 6.2's job).
- Reuse `InsertionModal.show(...)` unchanged for the composer's "+".

**Ask First:** none identified — session bootstrap is explicitly scoped to an in-memory value (see Design Notes) to avoid colliding with 6.2.

**Never:** the retry-tap action / `chat-messages-retry` call, offline composer banner/lock, multi-session switcher, bookmark/save-to-journal button, insight card (all Stories 6.2–6.5); rendering the SSE `context` event's retrieval/citation data; any direct AI-provider call.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Happy path | Session exists, backend streams `message_created→token*→done` | Bubble fills progressively, ends `complete` | N/A |
| Mid-stream drop | Connection closes after some tokens, no `done`/`error` | Bubble keeps partial text, status `failed`, generic error indicator (not retry copy) | `Failure.networkTimeout` surfaced, no exception escapes |
| In-band `error` event | SSE emits `error` with a taxonomy code | Message marked `failed` | `Failure.fromCode(code, message)` |
| Send while offline | No connectivity | Send fails immediately, bubble marked `failed` | `Failure.networkOffline` |
| Bootstrap failure | `chat-sessions-list`/`create` fails on screen open | Screen shows a generic error state, not infinite spinner | Failure surfaced, no crash |

</frozen-after-approval>

- The entries-owning feature's save port is idempotent on the save-to-journal identifier at the implementation level (not just the type signature) — a repeat save for the same source message never creates a second Entry.

# Step 2: Review

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`
- All review subagents must run at the same model capability as the current session.
- Run subagents synchronously: launch them together, then wait for all results before continuing.

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. The review layers are `{workflow.review_layers}`, resolved during activation.

2. For each layer in `{workflow.review_layers}`:
   - `instruction` empty or missing → drop the layer silently (an override disabled it).
   - `when` condition present and not satisfied by the current context (`{review_mode}`, `{spec_file}`) → drop the layer and tell the user, e.g. "Acceptance Auditor skipped — no spec file provided."
   - otherwise → the layer is active.

   If no layer is active, HALT with status `blocked` and blocking condition `no active review layers`.

3. Execute all active layers in parallel wherever their execution methods allow: expand `{skill-root}` in each layer's `instruction` to this skill's absolute installed directory, then substitute the runtime placeholders (`{diff_output}`, `{spec_file}`). For an instruction that launches a reviewer subagent, launch that child with the prompt text after placeholder substitution; do not load the reviewer instruction file yourself. For any other customized instruction, execute it as written. Do not leave `{skill-root}` unresolved in a child prompt. If a layer's instruction requires subagents and subagents are not available, for each such layer write under `{implementation_artifacts}` the exact child prompt from that layer's instruction after placeholder substitution (not a path-only pointer), then HALT. Ask the user to run each in a separate session (ideally a different LLM) and paste back the findings. When findings are pasted, treat them as those layers' findings and resume from this point. This is the only allowed parent-side read of a reviewer instruction file.

4. **Layer failure handling**: If any layer fails, times out, or returns empty results, append the layer's `name` to `{failed_layers}` (comma-separated) and proceed with findings from the remaining layers.

5. Collect all findings from the completed layers, keeping track of each finding's originating layer `id`.

# Step 3: Triage

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. **Normalize** findings from all layers into a unified list where each finding has:
   - `id` -- sequential integer
   - `source` -- the `id` of the layer that produced the finding (e.g., `blind-hunter`), or merged sources joined with `+` (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`)
   - `title` -- one-line summary
   - `detail` -- full description
   - `location` -- file and line reference (if available)

2. **Deduplicate.** Deduplicate only findings with the same claim and same required action. If two or more findings meet both conditions, merge them into one:
   - Use the most specific finding as the base (prefer findings with a precise location over prose-only findings).
   - Append any unique detail, reasoning, or location references from the other finding(s) into the surviving `detail` field.
   - Set `source` to the merged sources (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`).

3. Then evaluate each remaining finding independently. Do not reject a finding because a related finding was rejected.

input.new_string:
- Given a stream drops or returns an in-band error, when detected, then the partial bubble text is never cleared and no exception escapes the cubit.

### Review Findings

**Patch:**
- [ ] [Review][Patch] New `ApiClient.postStream`/`_mapStreamDioException` `AUTH_EXPIRED` → `SessionExpiryNotifier.notifyExpired()` branch has zero test coverage — the sibling non-stream path (`_mapDioException`) is fully covered by the existing Story 1.5 test group, but none of the 6 new `postStream` tests construct an `AUTH_EXPIRED` in-band stream error, so a regression in this duplicated branch (e.g. a mid-chat token expiry) would silently fail to surface the re-auth overlay with no test catching it. [lib/core/network/api_client.dart:171]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `ChatCubit.close()` cancels `_sendSubscription` without completing the in-flight `sendMessage()`'s `Completer` — `StreamSubscription.cancel()` never fires `onDone`/`onError`, so closing the cubit mid-send leaves that `Future` permanently unresolved (a leak, currently unobserved since no caller awaits it — see the related finding below). [lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:279-282]

[lib/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart:24-43,60-81]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `RetryInterceptor`'s new `neverRetriedFunctions` exclusion tests (`retry_interceptor_test.dart`) build `DioException`s with bare paths like `/chat-messages-send`, but the real call always goes through `pathParams: [sessionId]`, producing `/chat-messages-send/{sessionId}`. +  summary: The composer's client-side 8000-char cap (`TextField(maxLength: 8000, ...)`) assumes the backend counts `content` length the same way Flutter's `maxLength` does.

+  evidence: `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:253`. Review finding (code-review, blind-hunter layer). Nothing in this diff confirms the backend's own counting unit (bytes vs. code points vs. grapheme clusters), and this can't be verified from the client repo alone — same "can't verify without the other side's source" class as the `whisper_ggml`/`downloadModel` entry above. Revisit if surrogate-pair-heavy (emoji-heavy) messages are ever rejected despite passing the client-side check.
+  summary: No test drives an `authExpired` bootstrap failure through `ChatCubit`/`ChatScreen`.

+  evidence: `test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart`. Review finding (code-review, verification-gap layer). The underlying re-auth-overlay trigger is already covered generically by Story 1.5's `ApiClient._mapDioException` test group, which `listSessions`/`createSession`/`listMessages` all go through unchanged — so this is a thin-spot regression test for chat's own bootstrap path, not a live gap in the trigger mechanism itself.

+  summary: The streaming AI bubble (`ChatBubble`) renders growing text via plain `Text.rich` with no `Semantics(liveRegion: true)` — a screen-reader user gets no incremental announcement while tokens stream in.

+  evidence: `lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart`. Review finding (code-review, blind-hunter layer). Same unaddressed accessibility pattern already deferred for `Avatar`/nav icons/`EntryRecordCard` (Stories 1.2/1.6/4.1's own deferred-work entries) — no accessibility requirement is scoped for this story either; worth the same deliberate future pass.
+  summary: The two new `chat_sessions`/`chat_messages` Hive boxes accumulate every session/message ever fetched, with no eviction/TTL.

+  evidence: `lib/features/chat/chat_injection.dart`. Review finding (code-review, blind-hunter layer). Same unbounded-growth pattern already deferred for the `entries` Hive box (spec-4-1's own deferred-work entry) — not called out anywhere in the spec or epic-context as a future concern, so flagging here so it isn't forgotten once Story 6.2 (multi-session history) starts growing this data faster.
+  summary: `ChatCubit.sendMessage()`'s internal `await completer.future` is never awaited by its only caller (`ChatScreen._send()`), making the method effectively fire-and-forget from the UI.

+  evidence: `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:55`. Review finding (code-review, blind-hunter layer). Harmless today — nothing throws after that await point — but a future story (6.5's insight-trigger counting is the named candidate) adding logic after it inside `sendMessage()` would have its errors/results silently dropped unless the call site starts awaiting or the method's contract changes.
